title: Triage: central chest pain
body: Central chest pain radiating to the left arm, started about 30 minutes before arrival, with breathlessness. Pale and sweaty. Triage level 1. Oxygen started, ECG requested immediately and cardiology informed.

title: Cardiology assessment
body: Chest pain with breathlessness. ECG shows an abnormal rhythm. Started on antiplatelet therapy and continuous ECG monitoring. Repeat ECG and observations every 30 minutes.

sections.subjective: Crushing central chest pain, 8/10, radiating to left arm, short of breath.
sections.objective: HR 112, BP 146/92, SpO2 94% on oxygen. ECG: abnormal rhythm.
sections.plan: Aspirin 75 mg, continuous ECG monitoring, repeat ECG in 30 minutes, cardiology review.

title: Progress: pain settling
body: Pain now 2/10. Off oxygen with SpO2 98%. Remains on cardiac monitoring pending repeat ECG review.

title: Handover to General Medicine ward
body: Fever and dehydration. Temperature down from 39.2 to 37.8 after IV fluids and paracetamol. IV cannula re-sited at 09:55 after it came out during transfer. Tolerating oral fluids.

title: Neurology assessment: head injury after fall
body: Fall from a ladder of about 2.5 m onto concrete with a brief loss of consciousness. GCS 14 on arrival, pupils equal and reactive. CT head requested. Neurological observations every 30 minutes.

amendments.reason: Corrected fall height after speaking to family
amendments.previous_body: Fall from a ladder of about 2 m onto concrete with a brief loss of consciousness. GCS 14 on arrival, pupils equal and reactive. CT head requested. Neurological observations every 30 minutes.

title: Procedure: wrist immobilisation
body: X-ray confirms distal radius fracture. Left wrist immobilised in a below-elbow backslab. Distal pulses present and sensation intact after application. Fracture clinic follow-up arranged.

title: Assessment: acute abdominal pain
body: Severe right lower abdominal pain with vomiting and a temperature of 38.2. Tender in the right iliac fossa. Abdominal ultrasound requested, pain relief and antacid given, nil by mouth for now.

title: Progress: awaiting ultrasound
body: Pain improved to 4/10 and temperature settling. Ultrasound still pending. Surgical review to be requested if the scan is abnormal.

title: Discharge: allergic reaction
body: Urticarial rash resolved after antihistamine, no airway involvement. Observations back to normal and stable before discharge. Discharged with advice to avoid the suspected trigger and return if lip or tongue swelling or breathing difficulty develops.

title: Discharge: dizziness
body: Dizziness with a postural blood pressure drop, improved with oral and IV fluids. Blood glucose normal. Assisted fall on the ward at 11:50 without injury. Discharged with advice on fluids and to stand up slowly.

title: Assessment: acute breathlessness
body: Known asthma. Widespread wheeze, speaking in short phrases, SpO2 93% on oxygen. Nebulised salbutamol given and chest X-ray requested. Close monitoring of respiratory rate and oxygen saturation.

sections.subjective: Breathless since late morning, own inhaler not helping.
sections.objective: RR 24, HR 118, SpO2 93% on oxygen, peak flow 150 L/min.
sections.plan: Salbutamol 2.5 mg nebulised, oxygen to keep SpO2 94-98%, chest X-ray, reassess in 30 minutes.

title: Escalation: increased work of breathing
body: Respiratory rate up to 32 and SpO2 89% despite oxygen. Escalated to the doctor on duty, who attended within five minutes and repeated the nebuliser.

title: Procedure: burn dressing
body: Superficial burn of about 2% on the right forearm from hot cooking oil. Cooled, cleaned and covered with a non-adherent dressing. Dressing review in 48 hours.

title: Discharge: migraine
body: Typical migraine with photophobia and nausea, no red-flag features. Headache settled to 2/10 after an antiemetic and rest. Discharged with a headache diary and GP follow-up.
